claim: Macaques infected with barcoded SIVmac239 virus received cART beginning between 4 and 27 days post-infection.
source: In this study, macaques infected with a barcoded SIVmac239 virus received cART beginning between 4- and 27 days post-infection, leading to the establishment of different levels of viral dissemination and persistence.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract describing the experimental design.

claim: Later treatment initiation led to higher SIV DNA levels maintained during treatment.
source: Later treatment initiation led to higher SIV DNA levels maintained during treatment, which was significantly associated with an increased frequency of SIV reactivation and production of progeny capable of causing rebound viremia following treatment interruption.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental findings in the abstract.

claim: A 100-fold increase in SIV DNA in PBMCs was associated with only a 2-fold increase in the frequency of reactivation.
source: However, a 100-fold increase in SIV DNA in PBMCs was associated with only a 2-fold increase in the frequency of reactivation.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding stated in the abstract.

claim: The RCR can be established soon after infection.
source: These data suggest that the RCR can be established soon after infection, and that a large fraction of persistent viral DNA that accumulates after this time makes relatively little contribution to viral rebound.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data presented in the study, stated in the abstract.

claim: A large fraction of persistent viral DNA that accumulates after early infection makes relatively little contribution to viral rebound.
source: These data suggest that the RCR can be established soon after infection, and that a large fraction of persistent viral DNA that accumulates after this time makes relatively little contribution to viral rebound.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data presented in the study, stated in the abstract.

claim: Current treatment for HIV infection requires lifelong daily cART administration.
source: Current treatment for HIV infection requires an individual to undergo lifelong daily cART administration, as interruptions in dosing usually result in the rapid recrudescence of virus.
evidence: This is established knowledge about HIV treatment.

claim: Interruptions in cART dosing usually result in rapid recrudescence of virus.
source: Current treatment for HIV infection requires an individual to undergo lifelong daily cART administration, as interruptions in dosing usually result in the rapid recrudescence of virus.
evidence: This is established knowledge about HIV treatment outcomes.

claim: Viral recrudescence is thought to result from periodic activation of viral production from cells, including latently infected cells.
source: This viral recrudescence is thought to result from periodic activation of viral production from cells, including latently infected cells (Pinkevych et al., 2015; Fennessey et al., 2017), allowing the virus to spread to uninfected target cells no longer protected from infection by cART.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Different measures of the HIV reservoir often demonstrate a very wide range of values between individuals, varying between 100-fold and 1,000-fold.
source: These measures usually demonstrate a very wide range of values between individuals, varying between 100-fold and 1,000-fold for different individuals, and different measures are often poorly correlated (Eriksson et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Different measures of the HIV reservoir are often poorly correlated.
source: These measures usually demonstrate a very wide range of values between individuals, varying between 100-fold and 1,000-fold for different individuals, and different measures are often poorly correlated (Eriksson et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Groups of >100 individuals may be required to convincingly demonstrate even quite substantial changes in the reservoir size with treatment.
source: It has been estimated that groups of >100 individuals may be required to convincingly demonstrate even quite substantial changes in the reservoir size with treatment (Pinkevych et al., 2015; Moore et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The barcoded SIVmac239M virus contains approximately 10,000 clonotypes present at approximately equal proportions.
source: We previously developed a barcoded SIVmac239 virus, designated SIVmac239M, containing ≈10,000 clonotypes, present at approximately equal proportions (Fennessey et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental tool developed, supported by a citation.

claim: For animals treated starting on day 10 post-infection, the estimated frequency of reactivation from latency varied between 1.63 and 2.94 reactivations per day (mean = 2.29, SD = 0.47, n = 4).
source: For the four macaques treated starting on day 10 post-infection, the estimated frequency of reactivation from latency varied between 1.63 and 2.94 reactivations per day (mean = 2.29, SD = 0.47,n = 4).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the study.

claim: For animals treated beginning on day 27, the frequency of reactivation varied between 0.75 and 3.10 reactivations per day (mean 1.33, SD = 0.90, n = 5).
source: For animals treated beginning on day 27, the frequency varied between 0.75 and 3.10 reactivations per day (mean 1.33, SD = 0.90, n = 5) and was not significantly different from day 10 animals p=0.19 (Mann Whitney).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the study.

claim: The frequency of reactivation for day 27 treated animals was not significantly different from day 10 animals (p=0.19).
source: For animals treated beginning on day 27, the frequency varied between 0.75 and 3.10 reactivations per day (mean 1.33, SD = 0.90, n = 5) and was not significantly different from day 10 animals p=0.19 (Mann Whitney).
evidence: This is a statistical comparison of experimental results.

claim: The frequency of reactivation of animals treated on or after peak infection was significantly higher than animals treated at day four post-infection (Mann Whitney's p=0.0028).
source: The frequency of reactivation of animals treated on or after peak infection (pooled day 10 and day 27 groups) was significantly higher (Mann Whitney's p=0.0028) than the frequency of reactivation previously measured for animals treated at day four post-infection, which were between 0.40 and 0.87 per day (mean = 0.61, SD = 0.17, n = 6) (Figure 1h).
evidence: This is a statistical comparison of experimental results.

claim: Animals treated at day four post-infection had reactivation frequencies between 0.40 and 0.87 per day (mean = 0.61, SD = 0.17, n = 6).
source: The frequency of reactivation of animals treated on or after peak infection (pooled day 10 and day 27 groups) was significantly higher (Mann Whitney's p=0.0028) than the frequency of reactivation previously measured for animals treated at day four post-infection, which were between 0.40 and 0.87 per day (mean = 0.61, SD = 0.17, n = 6) (Figure 1h).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the study.

claim: Longer duration of treatment appeared to be associated with declining frequency of reactivation (half-life 216 days), although this was not significant (p=0.064).
source: Longer duration of treatment also appeared to be associated with declining frequency of reactivation (half-life 216 days), although this was not significant (p=0.064, linear mixed effects (LME) model) (Figure 1i).
evidence: This is a statistical analysis of experimental results.

claim: The levels of SIV gag DNA at interruption varied from <3.2 copies/10^6 PBMC among macaques treated beginning on day four to as many as 1000 DNA copies/10^6 PBMC among animals treated beginning on day 10.
source: The levels of SIV gag DNA at interruption varied over a wide range between cohorts, ranging from <3.2 copies/106 PBMC among macaques treated beginning on day four post-infection, to as many as 1000 DNA copies/106 PBMC among animals treated beginning on day 10 (Figure 2b).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the study.

claim: The level of log SIV DNA at treatment interruption was significantly correlated with the log frequency of reactivation (linear regression slope = 0.20, R2 = 0.56, p=0.0019).
source: When we correlated the level of log SIV DNA at treatment interruption with the log frequency of reactivation, we found a significant linear correlation (linear regression slope = 0.20, R2 = 0.56, p=0.0019)(Figure 2b).
evidence: This is a statistical analysis of experimental results.

claim: Day 27 treated animals had at least 116 fold higher SIV DNA level at interruption compared to day 4 treated animals.
source: Although the day 4 and day 27 treated animals were treated for a similar length of time (Figure 1b), the day 27 treated animals had at least 116 fold higher SIV DNA level at interruption, but only an approximately 2-fold difference in the frequency of reactivation with a mean of 0.61 (SD 0.17, n = 6) versus 1.33 (SD 0.90,n = 5) reactivations per day for day 4 and day 27 treated animals respectively.
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison of experimental results.

claim: Treatment later in infection was associated with a declining frequency of reactivation per DNA copy measured at treatment interruption.
source: This analysis showed that treatment later in infection was associated with a declining frequency of reactivation per DNA copy measured at treatment interruption (Figure 2c).
evidence: This is an analysis of experimental results.

claim: CA-RNA is not a significant predictor of post-ATI reactivation frequency (Pearson r of log-log transformed data is 0.37, p=0.18, n = 15).
source: Comparing reactivation rates with CA-RNA levels immediately prior to ATI, we find that CA-RNA is not a significant predictor of post-ATI reactivation frequency (Pearson r of log-log transformed data is 0.37, p=0.18, n = 15) (Figure 3b).
evidence: This is a statistical analysis of experimental results.

claim: Day 4-treated and d27-treated animals differed by 84 fold in their levels of SIV-CA RNA, despite only a two-fold difference in reactivation rate.
source: That is, the day 4-treated and d27-treated animals differed by 84 fold in their levels of SIV-CA RNA, despite only a two-fold difference in reactivation rate (Figure 3b).
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison of experimental results.

claim: Animals treated beginning at day 10 had higher immune activation just prior to treatment interruption than those treated on day 4 and 27.
source: Comparing animals treated beginning at day 4, 10 and day 27, we found that the animals treated beginning at day 10 had higher immune activation just prior to treatment interruption than those treated on day 4 and 27 (day 4 - mean (+ /- SD) Ki67 = 1.12%, (+ /- 0.38%), n = 6; day 10 – mean = 4.54%, (+ /- 1.87%), n = 4; day 27 – mean = 1.72%, (+ /- 0.39%), n = 5; however, only day 4 and day 10 groups were significantly different, Dunn's multiple comparisons test's p=0.005) (Figure 3d).
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison of experimental results with statistical analysis.

claim: Reactivation per SIV DNA copy was negatively correlated with the level of Ki67 expression (Spearman r −0.56, p=0.034).
source: Overall, cellular activation in PBMC did not seem a major driver of reactivation frequency, since reactivation per SIV DNA copy was negatively correlated with the level of Ki67 expression (Spearman r −0.56, p=0.034).
evidence: This is a statistical analysis of experimental results.

claim: The proportion of CD8+ T cells expressing CD107a in response to pooled SIV peptides was negatively correlated with the peak viral load observed during treatment interruption (Spearman r = −0.62, p=0.015, n = 15).
source: The proportion of CD8+ T cells expressing CD107a in response to pooled SIV peptides (measured at the time of treatment interruption) was negatively correlated with the peak viral load observed during treatment interruption (Spearman r = −0.62, p=0.015, n = 15).
evidence: This is a statistical analysis of experimental results.

claim: CD8+ T cells are able to mediate some level of immune control of SIV viral growth during rebound.
source: This suggests that CD8+ T cells are able to mediate some level of immune control of SIV viral growth during rebound (Figure 4c).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the correlation data.

claim: 50/60 sequences from the day 10 treated and 86/101 sequences from day 27 treated animals were intact and presumptively replication competent (mean of 84% intact, range of 75–100% in individual animals).
source: We found that 50/60 sequences from the day 10 treated and 86/101 sequences from day 27 treated animals were intact and presumptively replication competent (mean of 84% intact, range of 75–100% in individual animals).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from sequencing analysis.

claim: The majority of SIV sequences were intact, suggesting that differences in reactivation frequency cannot be explained by differences in replication competence.
source: Since the majority of sequences were intact, this suggests that differences in reactivation frequency cannot be explained by differences in replication competence.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the sequencing data.

claim: None of the peripheral immune or cytokine variables contributed significantly to the regression model for predicting reactivation frequency.
source: We found that none of the peripheral immune or cytokine variables contributed significantly to the regression model, indicating that these variables cannot accurately predict reactivation frequency.
evidence: This is a result from multiple regression analysis.

claim: The best model to predict reactivation frequency included both treatment duration and DNA levels at interruption (adjusted R2 = 0.73).
source: The best model to predict reactivation frequency included both treatment duration and DNA levels at interruption (adjusted R2 = 0.73).
evidence: This is a result from multiple regression analysis.

claim: Previous studies have demonstrated that latency is established very early after SIV infection.
source: Previous studies have demonstrated that latency is established very early after SIV infection (Whitney et al., 2014; Whitney et al., 2018; Okoye et al., 2018), consistent with our observations that seeding of the rebound competent viral reservoir is already established in macaques infected with a high-dose of virus and starting cART by day four post inoculation.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The frequency of reactivation from latency does not increase much beyond early infection, even though large increases in SIV CA-DNA and CA-RNA are observed accumulating in PBMC.
source: However, our study suggests that the frequency of reactivation from latency does not increase much beyond early infection, even though large increases in SIV CA-DNA and CA-RNA are observed accumulating in PBMC.
evidence: This is a summary of the study's findings.

claim: The majority of SIV reactivation events observed derive from a relatively small portion of the total proviral population, which can be established extremely early in infection.
source: It seems likely that the majority of SIV reactivation events observed derive from a relatively small portion of the total proviral population, which can be established extremely early in infection.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the study's findings.

claim: A subset of 0.4% of cells that is 100-fold more susceptible to infection and 500-fold more prone to reactivation could recapitulate the observed dynamics of DNA accumulation and post-ATI reactivation.
source: A subset of 0.4% of cells, that is 100-fold more susceptible to infection, and 500-fold more prone to reactivation (or a variety of combinations of these factors) could recapitulate the observed dynamics of DNA accumulation and post-ATI reactivation from the data (Figure 6).
evidence: This is a result from mathematical modeling.

claim: The peak viral load varied approximately 350 fold between animals starting treatment on day 4 and animals treated on day 27.
source: The peak viral load varied ≈350 fold between animals starting treatment on day 4 (geometric mean = 1.5×105 copies ml−1, CI of geo. mean (4.9 × 104, 4.4 × 105), n = 6) and animals treated on day 27 (geometric mean = 5.2×107 copies ml−1, CI of geo. mean (1.8 × 107, 1.5 × 108), n = 5).
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison of experimental results.

claim: The 'area under the curve' of viral exposure varied by >4,000 fold between day 4 and day 27 treated animals.
source: Similarly, the 'area under the curve' of viral exposure varied by >4,000 fold (geometric means 5.2 × 104, CI of geo. mean (1.8 × 104, 1.5 × 105) n = 6, vs 2.2 × 108, CI of geo. mean (1.3 × 108, 3.8 × 108), n = 5).
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison of experimental results.

claim: The prolonged viral replication led to an increase in SIV CA-DNA.
source: However, although the prolonged viral replication led to an increase in SIV CA-DNA (Archin et al., 2012), the additional exposure to virus between day 4 and 27 was associated with only approximately double the frequency of reactivation.
evidence: This is a result from the study, with a citation supporting the relationship between viral replication and CA-DNA.

claim: Only 2.4% of HIV proviral DNA is intact in patients starting cART in chronic infection.
source: Sequencing studies suggest that only 2.4% of HIV proviral DNA is intact in patients starting cART in chronic infection (Hiener et al., 2017; Bruner et al., 2016; Bruner et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Studies of SIVmac251 DNA in animals treated in chronic infection (95 weeks post-infection) for 36 weeks revealed that 28% remained intact.
source: Studies of SIVmac251 DNA in animals treated in chronic infection (95 weeks post-infection) for 36 weeks revealed that 28% remained intact (Bender et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Over the first year or two of infection, SIV DNA remains intact at much higher rates than HIV.
source: Thus, it appears that at least over the first year or two of infection, SIV DNA remains intact at much higher rates than HIV.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from comparing the study's data with cited HIV data.

claim: Extremely early treatment (with viral loads at treatment <1000–10,000 copies/ml) may severely restrict the establishment of the RCR.
source: Taken together, these data suggests that extremely early treatment (with viral loads at treatment <1000–10,000 copies/ml) may severely restrict the establishment of the RCR.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on comparing multiple studies.

claim: Once plasma viremia passes around 10,000 copies/ml the subsequent post-ATI frequency of reactivation is established.
source: However, once plasma viremia passes around 10,000 copies/ml the subsequent post-ATI frequency of reactivation is established.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on comparing multiple studies.

claim: Extending the duration of infection prior to starting cART (from day 4 to day 27) may greatly increase the level of proviral DNA and cell-associated RNA in PBMC, but does comparatively little to increase the frequency of reactivation.
source: Extending the duration of infection prior to starting cART (from day 4 to day 27) may greatly increase the level of proviral DNA (Archin et al., 2012) and cell-associated RNA in PBMC, but does comparatively little to increase the frequency of reactivation.
evidence: This is a summary of the study's findings.

claim: Recent studies have suggested that integrations sites and the propensity for clonal expansion of latent virus are similar between SIV and HIV.
source: However, recent studies have suggested that integrations sites and the propensity for clonal expansion of latent virus are similar between SIV and HIV (Ferris et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The initial inoculum of virus in the study is several orders of magnitude higher than that estimated in HIV.
source: The initial inoculum of virus in our studies is several orders of magnitude higher than that estimated in HIV (Keele et al., 2008), and thus this may disproportionately contribute to the early establishment and potential saturation of the SIV RCR.
evidence: This is a comparison with cited HIV data.

claim: Individuals treated very early during Fiebig stage one have only slightly longer average time to detection of plasma viral rebound than individuals starting treatment in chronic infection (median 26 vs. 14 days), despite considerably lower HIV DNA levels.
source: So while the case study of the Mississippi baby suggests that extremely early treatment can significantly delay viral rebound (Luzuriaga et al., 2015), Colby et al have recently shown that individuals treated very early during Fiebig stage one have only slightly longer average time to detection of plasma viral rebound than individuals starting treatment in chronic infection (median 26 vs. 14 days), despite considerably lower HIV DNA levels (Colby et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: A recent study showed that despite the overlap between provirus and QVOA, there was no overlap of either compartment with post-ATI rebound virus.
source: However, a recent study showed that despite the overlap between provirus and QVOA, there was no overlap of either compartment with post-ATI rebound virus (Lu et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Rebound virus originates from a different pool of cells to that reflected in circulating provirus.
source: This was taken to suggest that rebound virus originates from a different pool of cells to that reflected in circulating provirus.
evidence: This is an interpretation from a cited study.

claim: Most current measures of the HIV reservoir are measuring total CA-HIV or presumptively intact proviruses from PBMCs but not the major contributor to post-ATI rebound viremia.
source: Combined with our SIV results, it is clear that most current measures of the HIV reservoir are in fact measuring total CA-HIV or even presumptively intact proviruses from PBMCs (Bullen et al., 2014) but not the major contributor to post-ATI rebound viremia.
evidence: This is an interpretation combining the study's findings with cited research.

claim: The stability of the HIV reservoir has been measured in humans by measuring the decay of both HIV DNA and ex vivo inducible HIV, which were both found to decay with a half-life of >4 years.
source: The stability of the HIV reservoir has been measured in humans by measuring the decay of both HIV DNA and ex vivo inducible HIV, which were both found to decay with a half-life of >4 years (Besson et al., 2014; Siliciano et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: After 6 months of therapy, SIV DNA decays with a half-life of around 345 days.
source: Our study suggests that, after 6 months of therapy, SIV DNA decays with a half-life of around 345 days and SIV CA-RNA decays faster (half-life = 86 days, p<0.016, LME model).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the study.

claim: SIV CA-RNA decays with a half-life of 86 days (p<0.016).
source: Our study suggests that, after 6 months of therapy, SIV DNA decays with a half-life of around 345 days and SIV CA-RNA decays faster (half-life = 86 days, p<0.016, LME model).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the study.

claim: The frequency of reactivation declines with a half-life of approximately 216 days.
source: The frequency of reactivation declines slightly faster than SIV-DNA with a half-life of ≈216 days (although not significantly different, p=0.53, LME model).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the study.

claim: Reactivation frequency appears to decay at the same or faster rate than DNA levels in PBMC.
source: Thus, reactivation frequency appears to decay at the same or faster rate than DNA levels in PBMC.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the decay rate data.

claim: Total PBMC SIV CA-DNA is not the main determinant of post-treatment rebound.
source: This may be challenging, as our studies suggest that total PBMC SIV CA-DNA is not the main determinant of post-treatment rebound.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the study's findings.

claim: In total, 15 animals were intravenously infected with transfection produced SIVmac239M.
source: In total, 15 animals were intravenously infected with of transfection produced SIVmac239M as previously described (Fennessey et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design.

claim: 9 of 15 animals were infected with 2.2 × 10^5 IU and treated with cART at 4 and 27 dpi.
source: 9 of 15 animals were infected with 2.2 × 105 IU (1 mL) and treated with cART at 4 and 27dpi, while the remaining four animals were infected with 1 × 104 IU (1 mL) and treated with cART at 10dpi.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design.

claim: Four animals were infected with 1 × 10^4 IU and treated with cART at 10 dpi.
source: 9 of 15 animals were infected with 2.2 × 105 IU (1 mL) and treated with cART at 4 and 27dpi, while the remaining four animals were infected with 1 × 104 IU (1 mL) and treated with cART at 10dpi.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design.

claim: The limit of detection of the plasma viral load assay is 15 vRNA copies/mL.
source: The limit of detection of this assay is 15 vRNA copies/mL.
evidence: This is a technical specification of the assay used.
